title: console: nav visible CEL never evaluated and requiredPermissions ignores permission-set systemPermissions
body:
## Symptom

Neither of a navigation item's two gating fields can express "trim the menu by business role" in the console. Four controlled UI experiments (real logins per role):

1. `visible` (CEL, e.g. ``P`'org_admin' in current_user.positions` ``) is **never evaluated** — a constant-false predicate still renders for everyone.
2. `requiredPermissions` **is** evaluated (requiring a nonexistent name hides the item), but…
3. …it doesn't recognize capabilities granted via permission sets: requiring a capability hides the item from **everyone**, including holders of the permission set that declares it in `systemPermissions` and admins. In practice `requiredPermissions` degenerates into a "hide from everyone" switch.

Note: the server has returned the permission-set `systemPermissions` union from `/api/v1/auth/me/permissions` since 17.0.0-rc.0 — the client never consulted it.

## Root cause

- `evaluateVisibility` (app-shell) only evaluates `${…}` template strings. The `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelopes the spec's `ExpressionInputSchema` normalizes every authored `visible` string into fall through to a blanket `return true`.
- The sidebars' `checkPerm` maps a bare `requiredPermissions` name to `can(<name>, 'read')` — an object-CRUD check on a name that usually isn't an object — instead of the ADR-0066 capability subset check the server applies to `AppSchema.requiredPermissions`.

## Expected

`visible` CEL envelopes evaluate against `current_user` (positions etc. are already in the expression context); bare `requiredPermissions` names check the user's `systemPermissions` union, keeping the `object:action` form and the legacy object-read fallback.

Found via real-app dogfooding (os-tianshun-ehr platform defect registry PLAT-DEF-024, on 17.0.0-rc.0).
